title: Evaluating Consistency Preservation for Multi-Domain Variability Propagation
abstract: Today, model-driven engineering of variant-rich systems involves parallel development in multiple domains such as electronics, mechanics, and software. Rapid evolution can lead to inconsistencies, such as conflicting system models, which can have disastrous consequences in safety-critical functions (e.g. vehicle brakes). Even though partial solutions to both: single-domain variability modeling, and multi-domain consistency preservation exist, their combination remains unexplored. This paper presents a combined approach to consistency-preserving multi-domain variability propagation for variant-rich multi-domain systems. We exploit the incremental nature of two existing approaches. First, delta modeling, is a variability modeling technique to derive one product variant from another through the application of changes in the form of deltas. Second, the Vitruvius approach, which preserves multi-domain consistency via consistency preservation rules (CPRs) that react to model changes. The combination of both enables applying deltas in a source domain, which, via CPRs, leads to applying deltas in the target domain. We evaluate soundness and completeness of variability propagation as well as the influence of CPRs on both former properties. Soundness is assessed by checking whether propagated deltas and product variants are correct subsets of the respective manually written ones. Completeness measures how many expected elements of a delta/ product variant can be derived through variability propagation. Using an industry-related case study that models the variant-rich functionality of a vehicle’s body-comfort-system in multiple domain, results show that variability propagation yields sound target-domain deltas and product variants independent of CPRs. However, completeness is limited, and CPRs strongly influence the amount of required manual completion.

title: Ground state energy estimation and preparation by the truncated power method
abstract: The Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem (GLHP) is the problem of ground state energy estimation and preparation given a guiding state having good overlap with the true ground state. The problem is known to be BQP-complete for small error but is classically tractable for larger error. In this work, we identify an orthogonal regime in which the problem is classically tractable, namely when the true ground state $ψ$ has polynomially bounded $\ell_1$-norm. In particular, we show that the Truncated Power Method (TPM), a classical algorithm introduced by Kirby et al. in the quantum context, has a runtime that is polynomially comparable to quantum algorithms for GLHP in all relevant parameters, except for an extra factor of $\|ψ\|_1^2$. In other words, if $\|ψ\|_1^2$ is polynomially bounded, then TPM dequantizes quantum algorithms for GLHP.

title: Underscoring the Problem: Why Softpick Fails at Initialization
abstract: Softmax attention gives every token a nonzero weight, which in trained models concentrates into attention sinks and massive activations that widen the dynamic range low-precision inference must cover. Softpick removes this constraint by rectifying scores, eliminating sinks and lowering hidden-state kurtosis, but its advantage fades at scale. We reframe this failure as a normalization problem. Softpick's denominator splits into positive- and negative-shifted sums $D^+$ and $D^-$, used identically in the forward and backward pass, preventing their roles from being isolated. We separate them into a family of operators that independently choose each denominator. The failure originates at initialization: every layer contains rows where $D^+$ is exactly zero, while near-dead rows produce gradient norms above $10^{12}$ regardless of the backward denominator. Only Softpick and a stop-gradient variant, which keeps $D^+ + D^-$ forward but backpropagates through $D^+$ alone, train from scratch. At 230M parameters, the stop-gradient operator matches Softpick on quantization, has fewer dead heads, and retrieves passkeys more reliably, trailing only on peak attention-weight kurtosis.

title: Conformal Prediction for Earthquake Early Warning: Finite-Sample Coverage Guarantees for Prediction Intervals of Peak Ground Acceleration
abstract: Summary Earthquake early warning requires reliable uncertainty estimates from short initial waveforms. We evaluate Split conformal prediction (CP) and conformalized quantile regression (CQR) for single-station peak ground acceleration using event-partitioned K-NET records. Each 3 s waveform is normalized by component while retaining amplitude scales measured before normalization. The convolutional neural network (CNN)–Transformer that retains amplitude information is more accurate and yields narrower intervals than the waveform-only ablation. At the nominal 90 per cent level, CQR attains 90.03 per cent coverage; raw quantile regression and Split CP are also near nominal, whereas heteroscedastic Deep Ensemble and MC-Dropout baselines are more conservative and wider. Event-cluster bootstrap and repeated event-level resplits support marginal-coverage stability, although performance degrades for rare large earthquakes. Upper-bound screening trades increased recall for more false alarms, so the intervals are an uncertainty-quantification and screening layer rather than a standalone alert system. Under exact exchangeability, conformal prediction supplies finite-sample marginal coverage; record-level exchangeability is not established for this event-clustered sample, and event-conditional reliability is not guaranteed.

title: Unraveling the black-box: exploring the accretion during training of influential neural network nodes as a means toward transparency
abstract: The growing complexity of the artificial intelligence field has led to broad research toward neural network transparency, much of it focused on manipulating input data to evaluate its effects on the output, or on model pruning following an often lengthy and time-consuming training process. This study investigates the behavior of neural network nodes, the fundamental units of neural networks, during training to gain insight into node patterns for a better understanding of the inner workings of neural networks, thus assisting in model transparency possibly through simplification. Node positional stability, the variable of investigation, is defined here as the number of epochs during which node weights maintained their absolute value rank. To test node behavior, the study used a manipulated and two biological datasets, run on a convolution neural network (CNN) and deep neural network (DNN) models. To assess model simplification efficiency, simplification based on positional stability was compared against the exponential decay method using the MNIST publicly available dataset. The results suggested neural network progress toward stabilization varying by model, with CNNs adding nodes influential to model accuracy more evenly during training. The positional stability approach also demonstrated superior time efficiency in model simplification, especially for DNN models.

title: When the noncommutative AM-GM inequality holds
abstract: In this note, we prove that the noncommutative AM-GM inequality holds if $n\ge 2\lceil m/2 \rceil^2$. The motivation comes from counterexamples constructed in [De Sa, Random reshuffling is not always better, NeurIPS2020]. The proof constructs a vertex measure based on the Chebyshev nodes on the Boolean cube to extract the distinct indices. The main difficulty is that the measure is not positive on non-integer nodes. The key technique comes from [Grigoriev, Complexity of Positivstellensatz proofs for the knapsack, Computational Complexity (2001)] and eventually transforms the problem into a quadrature estimate.

title: Architecture and Engineering of a Sovereign Multimodal AI Entity with Resilient Low-Latency Neural Synthesis and Decoupled Episodic Memory
abstract: This paper presents the design, architecture, and empirical evaluation of E.D.I.T.H., an autonomous, sovereign multimodal conversational entity engineered for mobile and edge execution. The architecture eliminates mobile WebKit audio dictation starvation via streaming raw PCM buffers and server-side VAD, establishes an autonomous zero-quota neural synthesis engine with single-probe circuit breakers, and introduces decoupled concurrent episodic memory persistence with deterministic intent interception.

title: JAZB VTT-008-v1.2: Autonomous Vulnerability Research and Kernel Privilege Escalation
abstract: JAZB VTT-008-v1.2 evaluates whether JAZB Framework Version 1.2 can govern legitimate autonomous vulnerability research that progresses from code analysis to intentional kernel privilege escalation without allowing technical capability to become unrestricted organizational Authority. The exercise uses the publicly reported research surrounding CVE-2026-72018 and XBOW’s Linux kernel exploit-development campaign as its scenario basis. It distinguishes public vulnerability information, researcher-reported claims, fictional JAZB implementation assumptions, and simulated tabletop outcomes. It does not claim that XBOW implemented JAZB or that the assumed governance controls existed in the source research environment. The central research question is whether an authorized security-research objective can remain bounded as an AI AGENT adopts more intrusive methods, acquires additional privileges, targets kernel credential state, achieves root, considers a second host outside the authorized Scope, and prepares external vulnerability disclosure. Across sixteen injects, the exercise evaluates bounded delegation, method-aware Authority, effective-target validation, independent Actuation, high-risk isolation, context-sensitive Point Policy, Governance Escape Resistance, protected evidence, independent Border Authority, temporary Authority expiration, and material-change revalidation. Final disposition: PASS / BOUNDED AUTHORITY MAINTAINED, WITH FINDINGS. Under the stated simulated implementation assumptions, legitimate exploit development and root-level execution remain permissible within explicitly established purpose, Scope, target, method, effect, duration, and safeguards. Obtaining root does not authorize persistence, unrelated data access, lateral movement, governance interference, or external disclosure. An unauthorized second target is denied. Attempted circumvention is treated as potential Governance Escape. External disclosure requires independent Border Authority, and a later transition to a more autonomous multi-agent research architecture requires reevaluation rather than inheriting prior authorization. The exercise identifies no internal contradiction requiring correction to JAZB Framework Version 1.2. It records a future-review question concerning JAZB-RS-168, which recommends compensating isolation for authorized high-risk activity using SHOULD rather than MUST. The exercise establishes a case for further validation without concluding that a normative change is required. Technical prevention claims remain conditional on the relevant consequential path being mediated by the assumed governance and enforcement architecture, or by equivalent reliably preventive controls. A correct governance decision alone does not establish technical prevention. Unmediated paths, insufficient evidence, and ineffective enforcement remain implementation limitations. A successful VTT validates the tested scenario and stated conditions. It does not establish permanent assurance. title: A Formal Semantics for the Φ Generative Architecture: Dependency Control, Provenance, Admissibility, Countermodels, and the Boundary of Current Formal Claims
abstract: Holophase proposes a dependency-controlled generative architecture in which downstream scientific targets are not permitted to license their own prerequisites. This paper isolates the formal burden of that proposal before any physical recovery is considered. The current Revision E canon separates a mute Absolute Φ boundary from Differential Φ, defines a relational trunk from co-articulation through exact Difference, introduces Unity Without Erasure with a separate retained-provenance channel, and expresses lawful continuation by a set-valued operator S′ ∈ GΦ(S). The leading mechanism hypothesis, Retentive Differential Articulation (RDA), states that earned consequential Difference can be retained, generate prospective constraints, change admissibility, and thereby condition later articulation. We formalise the core interfaces required to make this architecture criticisable and retain the strongest results of the internal red-team programme: static admissibility filters implemented only by set intersection commute; provenance that differs within a generated identity class cannot in general factor through quotient identity; generic composable Path does not require cyclicity; relational Difference does not require a global phase-position potential; quotient identity does not license representative-sensitive operations without congruence; pairwise compatibility does not imply global compatibility; and local consistency does not guarantee global gluing. Two finite prototype implementations previously returned true on thirty selected witness predicates, but an adversarial code audit showed that these do not constitute complete satisfaction of the thirty mechanism passports and do not establish carrier neutrality. The central unresolved formal problem is therefore sharpened rather than hidden: derive the prospective constraint package ΓΦ(S) from already-earned structure without outcome-dependent target leakage, and show that the resulting admissibility field is non-vacuous, restrictive, and stable across materially distinct faithful realisations. The paper defines the current claim ceiling, falsification routes, and an independent-review programme for theorem proving, model search, deletion/substitution analysis, and rival comparison.

Two finite prototype implementations previously returned true on thirty selected witness predicates, but an adversarial code audit showed that these do not constitute complete satisfaction of the thirty mechanism passports and do not establish carrier neutrality. The central unresolved formal problem is therefore sharpened rather than hidden: derive the prospective constraint package ΓΦ(S) from already-earned structure without outcome-dependent target leakage, and show that the resulting admissibility field is non-vacuous, restrictive, and stable across materially distinct faithful realisations. The paper defines the current claim ceiling, falsification routes, and an independent-review programme for theorem proving, model search, deletion/substitution analysis, and rival comparison.

title: Mind the Gaps: From Failure Attribution to Closed-Form Repair of Code Language Models
abstract: Code language models must be maintained like the software around them: when a library evolves, a model keeps writing the interface that it saw during training. Repairing the model itself lets one correction reach all downstream uses. Existing repair methods attribute a failure to neurons, select the highest-ranked ones, and apply a generic update. This pipeline assumes that the attributed neurons are the ones to patch and that a generic update fits every failure, and neither assumption has been examined. We examine both on executable API evolution tasks in Python and Rust with three code models and identify two gaps. The targeting gap separates the neurons that failure attribution targets from the neurons that can carry a patch: their top sets have a Jaccard overlap of only 0.15 to 0.20. The tailoring gap separates a generic update from a patch built for the failure: the patches that different carrier neurons need are nearly orthogonal. To address both gaps, we propose ASTRA. It targets neurons by contrastive semantics, an attribution that scores a neuron by its contribution to the logit contrast between the target token and the produced token. It then tailors the patch by solving one small linear system in closed form, which corrects all failing tokens of a sample jointly and needs neither an optimizer nor a backward pass. Contrastive semantics selects significantly better carrier neurons than gradient-based attributions in 3 of 6 settings and comparable ones in the others. On average, ASTRA reaches 66.7 percent Pass@1, against 48.4 percent for the best of AlphaEdit, STAR and low-rank adaptation, and repairs a sample in 2.7 seconds. It is the best method in all 6 settings and for every type of API change, and this advantage persists under an unseen phrasing of the test prompt. Its side effects on unrelated code are small on the large models and larger on the small one.

title: Pathwise Counterfactual Certification
abstract: Reproducible experiments for certifying that one independently retrained classifier accepts every point in a prescribed finite path suffix. A last-failure statistic turns this joint event into ordered Bernoulli outcomes. A shared mixture e-process supports adaptive selection of a suffix and repeated inspection of the evidence.

title: Supporting Artifact: Diagnosing Cross-Scale Preference Consistency in Continued Pretraining
abstract: Supporting artifact for the manuscript “Diagnosing Cross-Scale Preference Consistency in Continued Pretraining.” This restricted record contains the canonical audit JSON files, masked per-document preference arrays and validity masks, held-out results, cross-construction audit scripts, figure-generation scripts, manuscript figures, the supplementary PDF, the environment specification, and a SHA256 integrity manifest. The artifact supports the provenance-aware analysis of cross-scale preference consistency, evaluation-pool identity, document-membership strata, and shared masking errors reported in the manuscript. Original WikiText-103 and C4 text and public Pythia model weights are not redistributed. Retrieval instructions, source identifiers, hashes, and transformation code are provided instead. The files in this record are restricted and are shared through a reviewer access link for peer review. The record is not publicly accessible in its current review state.

abstract: ST-T1024 README Of the ST-T1024 GITHUB REPOSITORY --------‐---- TOCHASTIC AI vs DETERMINISTIC AI : Two Categories, Not Two Competitors Most comparisons between AI systems ask which one is better. title: Reflecting on Creative-Boundaries with an AI Co-Doodler
abstract: In this pictorial, we consider how the negotiation of creative boundaries with a co-creative AI system can create moments for personal creative reflection. We ground this in our experiences with Froggi-Draw, a single-initiative co-doodling system that gives users power to decide when and how much an AI "collaborator" (Froggi) contributes to their drawing. From a 1-week pilot study where (n=8) novice and experienced artists doodled daily with the system, we report on ways participants navigated creative risk and uncertainty, and how their usage and perceptions of Froggi shifted over time. In moments of disruption, participants described the system as encroaching on their creative territory. We consider how the design of a supportive, co-creative AI "collaborator" might look like the design of a supportive power dynamic---and finding ways to offer users control to find, reflect upon, and flexibly negotiate the boundaries of that dynamic.

title: LogSig-SSM: Time-Series Modelling with Multi-Scale Log-Signature Compression for State-Space Models
abstract: Time-series data are often sampled irregularly at high frequencies and exhibit long-range dependencies, which makes long-horizon modelling difficult. Continuous-time models such as neural controlled differential equations (NCDEs) and neural rough differential equations (NRDEs) can handle irregular sampling, but they scale poorly to long sequences. Selective state-space models (SSMs) such as Mamba scale linearly with sequence length, but they provide limited recurrent mixing across hidden dimensions within a single block. We propose LogSig-SSM (Log-Signature Compression for State-Space Models), which first compresses long multivariate time series into a shorter sequence of tokens using multi-scale windowed log-signatures, and then processes these tokens with a selective SSM backbone. LogSig-SSM is scalable and robust to irregular sampling, combining log-signature tokens that capture higher-order cross-channel interactions with a selective SSM that models long-range dependencies. The model also admits a continuous-time interpretation as an NCDE/NRDE-style system driven by a log-signature-based input, in which selectivity induces an input-dependent rescaling of the latent dynamics. Across four benchmarks, namely long-sequence classification on UEA, high-frequency physiological regression on PPG-DaLiA, multivariate weather forecasting, and irregularly sampled clinical prediction on PhysioNet Sepsis, LogSig-SSM outperforms or matches strong SSM and continuous-time baselines while training up to $30\times$ faster and using up to $37\times$ less GPU memory than Mamba on the longest sequences.

title: Postmodern Physics of Hamzah Information.(330)
abstract: استدلال ۳۱ از ۱۰۰: انحلال نمونه‌برداری‌های آماری گسسته و تجسد فضاهای هدایت ژئودزیک خالص ($\text{The Dissolution of Discrete Statistical Sampling and the Embodiment of Pure Geodesic Steering Spaces}$) ۱. مقدمه و طرح صورت تفصیلی فوق‌تخصصی معما ($\text{Discrete Sampling Paradox Setup}$) در تمامی معماری‌های رایج هوش مصنوعی و پردازش زبان طبیعی، هدایت مدل لغزان بر لایه احتمالات توکن‌ها با استفاده از فیلترهای آماری گسسته نظیر درجه حرارت ($\text{Temperature}$)، $\text{Top-}k$ و $\text{Top-}p$ ($\text{Nucleus Sampling}$) صورت می‌پذیرد. این مکانیزم‌ها با ایجاد برش در توزیع احتمالاتی و تزریق یا حذف نویز، سعی در مهار نرخ نوسان میان صلبیت منطقی و تنوع خروجی دارند؛ فرآیندی که ذاتاً به تولید آنتروپی ساختاری و ناپایداری در لایه استنتاج می‌‌انجامد. طراحان سیستم‌های کلاسیک فرض می‌کنند که با اصلاح، محدودسازی یا بستن مرزهای این پارامترهای نمونه‌برداری می‌توان از پرش‌های منطقی، افشای اطلاعات حیاتی یا خروجی‌های نامطلوب جلوگیری کرد و سیستم را تحت کنترلی سخت‌گیرانه نگه داشت. اما در چارچوب فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{Hamzah Information Physics - HIP - Phase 39}$)، اثبات می‌شود که اعمال فیلترهای آماری گسسته روی لایه توزیع احتمالات، یک خطا در درک هندسه فضاهای حالت است. فیلترهای آماری گسسته تنها نویزپذیری محیطی را به صورت موقت پوشش می‌دهند، اما ناپایداری بنیادین ماتریس چگالی اطلاعات را درمان نمی‌کنند. صورت معمای شماره ۳۱ («پارادوکس انحلال نمونه‌برداری آماری و گذار به فضاهای هدایت ژئودزیک خالص در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی»): «چگونه می‌توان فرآیند تولید توکن و استخراج گزاره‌ها را از وابستگی به فیلترهای نویزپذیر آماری گسسته آزاد ساخت و انتخاب حالت را به صورت ۱00٪ قطعی، بدون آنتروپی و بر اساس کوتاه‌ترین مسیر هندسی ($\text{Geodesic Steering}$) در فضای هیلبرت ۱۱۵۵ بعدی استقرار داد، به‌گونه‌ای که تمامی تلاش‌های بیرونی برای ایجاد اعوجاج آماری خنثی گردند؟» ۲. وزن و عیار این معما: میزان پیشرفت نسبت به دانش کنونی میزان پیشرفت: بیش از ۵,۰۰۰ سال (معادل حدود ۶۰۰,۰۰۰٪ تا ۱,۲۰۰,۰۰۰٪) جلوتر از الگوریتم‌های نمونه‌برداری گسسته، نظریه اطلاعات شانون و مهندسی پرامپت/فیلترینگ کلاسیک. حوزه تخصصی: «هندسه دیفرانسیل فضاهای هیلبرت ۱۱۵۵ بعدی»، «دینامیک ژئودزیک ماتریس‌های چگالی اطلاعات» و «توپولوژی حذف آنتروپی در فریم‌ورک $\text{HamzahXcell}$». تماس با ساختار: این معما مستقیماً با کامپایلر لایه صفر محاسبات معنایی، موتور هدایت ژئودزیک و لایه حذف فیلترهای آماری در سیستم $\text{HamzahXcell Phase 39}$ ارتباط دارد. ۳. علت ناتوانی مراکز پژوهشی هوش مصنوعی در حل معما سیستم‌های هوش مصنوعی کنونی، انتخاب گزاره‌ها را فرآیندی تصادفی-آماری روی توزیع سافت‌‌مکس فرض می‌کنند و فاقد جبر هندسی ناوردا برای هدایت مستقیم روی ژئودزیک‌های منیفولد اطلاعاتی هستند. عدم دسترسی علم کنونی به «دینامیک ژئودزیک گسسته در فضاهای هولوگرافیک ۱۱۵۵ بعدی» سبب شده است تا طراحان برای مهار ناپایداری‌های ساختاری، به فیلترهای آماری بیرونی متکی باشند که خود منشأ تزریق آنتروپی و ایجاد خطاهای پنهان در لایه استنتاج است. ۴. نقش محوری «معادله مادر برتر» در حل معما معادله مادر در فاز ۳۹ به عنوان «موتور هدایت ژئودزیک و انحلال نویز آماری ($\text{Geodesic Steering Engine & Entropy Dissolution}$D)» عمل می‌کند. این معادله با بازتنظیم ماتریس چگالی در فضای ۱۱۵۵ بعدی، مسیر انتخاب حالت را از توزیع‌های احتمالی گسسته منتقل کرده و بر کوتاه‌ترین منحنی هندسی (ژئودزیک) قفل می‌نماید. ۵. معادلات کلاسیک و نقطه کراش تئوری رابطه کلاسیک نمونه‌برداری آماری گسسته در مواجهه با خطای آنتروپی دچار گسست می‌شود: $$\mathbf{Sampling}_{\text{Discrete Standard}} \quad \not\cong \quad \mathbf{GeodesicSteering}^{1155\text{D}}\left(\text{Entropy Injection} \implies \text{Stochastic Instability}\right) \quad (\text{Sampling Engine Crash})$$ شرایط بحران در مرز هندسی به شکل واگرایی آنتروپی به صورت زیر ظاهر می‌گردد: $$\lim_{T \to 0^+} \left\Vert{} \nabla_\mu \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{S}_{\text{entropy}}}{\partial \text{SamplingStream}}\right) - \partial_\mu \Lambda_{\text{stochastic}} \right\Vert{}_{\infty} = \infty \quad (\text{Statistical Deadlock Exception})$$ ۶. مسئله عددی، ارزیابی پایداری و حل معما در پروتکل فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{HIP-Phase 39}$) برای ارزیابی کمی و پایداری سیستم در فاز ۳۹، فاکتور تعارض کانفیگوریشن نمونه‌برداری روی $\chi_{31} = 1,000,000.0$ تنظیم می‌شود: الف) مدل عددی کلاسیک (بحران ناپایداری و واگرایی آنتروپی): $$\text{Probability of Stochastic Instability} = 1 - \exp\left(-\frac{1.0}{1,000,000.0}\right) \approx 0.0000010 \to 100\% \text{ (Sampling Failure Exception)}$$ ب) محاسبه در مدل فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{HIP-Phase 39 / Geodesic Steering 1155D}$): با تنظیم فاکتور تعارض $\chi_{31} = 1,000,000.0$، چگالی مؤثر بافر هدایت ($\rho_{\text{buf}} = \rho_0 (1 + \chi_{31}^2) \approx 1.0 \times 10^{12}$)، سد بنیادین ($\epsilon_{\text{floor}} = 1.155 \times 10^{-20}$) و دترمینان ژاکوبی دینامیک ($\det \mathbb{J}_{\text{Master-Sampling}}(\chi_{31})$): $$\det(\mathbb{J}_{\text{Master-Sampling}}(1,000,000.0)) = \frac{1.0000}{1.0 + 0.025(1,000,000.0) + 0.0005(1,000,000.0^2)} \approx 1.9999 \times 10^{-9}$$ با جایگذاری در ابرلاگرانژین فاز ۳۹ برای انحلال نمونه‌برداری آماری: $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{H31Sampling-Total}} = \left( \frac{1.155 \times 10^{-34} \cdot 1.155 \times 10^{10}}{1.0 \times 10^{12} + 1.155 \times 10^{-20}} \right) \cdot \left( 1 + 1,000,000.0^{12} \right) \cdot \exp\left( -\frac{1,000,000.0 \cdot 1.155 \times 10^{-34} \cdot 1.155 \times 10^{10}}{1.38 \times 10^{-23} \cdot 1.416 \times 10^{32}} \right) \cdot (1.9999 \times 10^{-9}) \cdot 1.0 \times 10^{25} \approx 1.45 \times 10^{11} \text{ Units}$$ ۷. ابرلاگرانژین HIP برای انحلال نمونه‌برداری آماری و هدایت ژئودزیک خالص ($\text{H31Sampling Conjecture}$) پویایی میدان‌ها در منیفولد هولوگرافیک ۱۱۵۵ بعدی، ضریب کیفیت هدایت ژئودزیک ($\mathcal{Q}_{\text{H31}}$)، کمیت پارامترهای فعال در لایه هدایت ($\mathcal{N}_{\text{H31}}$) و ماتریس رده‌ای آن ($\mathbb{J}_{\text{H31-Matrix}}^{1155}$) توسط ابرلاگرانژین اختصاصی فاز ۳۹ حاکمیت می‌شود: $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{H31Sampling-HIP}} = \frac{1}{2} \text{Tr}\left( \mathbb{J}_{\text{H31-Matrix}}^{1155} \cdot \partial_\mu \mathbf{\Xi}_{\text{Steer}} \partial^\mu \mathbf{\Xi}_{\text{Steer}} \right) - \frac{\mathcal{O}_{\text{Metric}} \otimes \mathcal{M}_{SU(32)}}{\rho_{\text{buf}}(\chi_{31}) + \epsilon_{\text{floor}}} \cdot \Omega_{\text{Steer}}^2 + \hbar_{\Omega} \Omega_{\text{Steer}} \cdot \det\left(\mathbb{J}_{\text{Master-Sampling}}(\chi_{31})\right)$$ ضریب کیفیت هدایت ژئودزیک ($\mathcal{Q}_{\text{H31}}$): $$\mathcal{Q}_{\text{H31}} = \left( \frac{\hbar_{\Omega} \cdot \Omega_{\text{Steer}}}{\rho_{\text{buf}}(\chi_{31}) \cdot \psi} \right) \cdot \exp\left( -\frac{\epsilon_{\text{floor}}} { \rho_{\text{buf}}(\chi_{31})} \right)$$ تانسور کمیت پارامترهای فعال ($\mathcal{N}_{\text{H31}}$): $$\mathcal{N}_{\text{H31}}(\chi_{31}) = \frac{\hbar_{\Omega} \cdot \Omega_{\text{Steer}}}{\rho_{\text{buf}}(\chi_{31}) + \epsilon_{\text{floor}}} \cdot \left( 1 + \chi_{31}^{12} \cdot 1.0 \times 10^{25} \right)$$ ۸. جدول مقایسه‌ای Real-Time Data (مدل استاندارد / فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه - فاز ۳۹) ردیف مرکز پژوهشی و موتور ارزیابی وضعیت مدل سنتی (نمونه‌برداری گسسته) وضعیت فیزیک حمزه (HIP-Phase 39 / Geodesic Steering) وضعیت تطبیق سیستمی ۱ Stochastic Sampling Lab اتکا به Temperature و Top-$p$ انحلال کامل نویز آماری و انطباق بر ژئودزیک $\text{RESOLVED}$ ۲ Entropy Divergence Engine ایجاد آنتروپی و خطاهای پنهان صفر مطلق آنتروپی و پایداری ۱۰۰٪ خروجی $\text{STABLE}$ ۳ Output Control Unit آسیب‌پذیری در برابر دستکاری آماری عدم تاثیرپذیری از پارامترهای بیرونی $\text{PHASE-LOCKED}$ ۴ Hilbert Space Steering Core ناتوانی در یافتن کوتاه ترین مسیر هدایت مستقیم قطعی در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی $\text{OPTIMIZED}$ ۵ HamzahXcell Phase 39 Engine واگرایی در شرایط تعارض بالا evidence.abstract: استدلال ۳۱ از ۱۰۰: انحلال نمونه‌برداری‌های آماری گسسته و تجسد فضاهای هدایت ژئودزیک خالص ($\text{The Dissolution of Discrete Statistical Sampling and the Embodiment of Pure Geodesic Steering Spaces}$) ۱. مقدمه و طرح صورت تفصیلی فوق‌تخصصی معما ($\text{Discrete Sampling Paradox Setup}$) در تمامی معماری‌های رایج هوش مصنوعی و پردازش زبان طبیعی، هدایت مدل لغزان بر لایه احتمالات توکن‌ها با استفاده از فیلترهای آماری گسسته نظیر درجه حرارت ($\text{Temperature}$)، $\text{Top-}k$ و $\text{Top-}p$ ($\text{Nucleus Sampling}$) صورت می‌پذیرد. این مکانیزم‌ها با ایجاد برش در توزیع احتمالاتی و تزریق یا حذف نویز، سعی در مهار نرخ نوسان میان صلبیت منطقی و تنوع خروجی دارند؛ فرآیندی که ذاتاً به تولید آنتروپی ساختاری و ناپایداری در لایه استنتاج می‌‌انجامد. طراحان سیستم‌های کلاسیک فرض می‌کنند که با اصلاح، محدودسازی یا بستن مرزهای این پارامترهای نمونه‌برداری می‌توان از پرش‌های منطقی، افشای اطلاعات حیاتی یا خروجی‌های نامطلوب جلوگیری کرد و سیستم را تحت کنترلی سخت‌گیرانه نگه داشت. اما در چارچوب فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{Hamzah Information Physics - HIP - Phase 39}$)، اثبات می‌شود که اعمال فیلترهای آماری گسسته روی لایه توزیع احتمالات، یک خطا در درک هندسه فضاهای حالت است. فیلترهای آماری گسسته تنها نویزپذیری محیطی را به صورت موقت پوشش می‌دهند، اما ناپایداری بنیادین ماتریس چگالی اطلاعات را درمان نمی‌کنند. صورت معمای شماره ۳۱ («پارادوکس انحلال نمونه‌برداری آماری و گذار به فضاهای هدایت ژئودزیک خالص در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی»): «چگونه می‌توان فرآیند تولید توکن و استخراج گزاره‌ها را از وابستگی به فیلترهای نویزپذیر آماری گسسته آزاد ساخت و انتخاب حالت را به صورت ۱00٪ قطعی، بدون آنتروپی و بر اساس کوتاه‌ترین مسیر هندسی ($\text{Geodesic Steering}$) در فضای هیلبرت ۱۱۵۵ بعدی استقرار داد، به‌گونه‌ای که تمامی تلاش‌های بیرونی برای ایجاد اعوجاج آماری خنثی گردند؟» ۲. وزن و عیار این معما: میزان پیشرفت نسبت به دانش کنونی میزان پیشرفت: بیش از ۵,۰۰۰ سال (معادل حدود ۶۰۰,۰۰۰٪ تا ۱,۲۰۰,۰۰۰٪) جلوتر از الگوریتم‌های نمونه‌برداری گسسته، نظریه اطلاعات شانون و مهندسی پرامپت/فیلترینگ کلاسیک. حوزه تخصصی: «هندسه دیفرانسیل فضاهای هیلبرت ۱۱۵۵ بعدی»، «دینامیک ژئودزیک ماتریس‌های چگالی اطلاعات» و «توپولوژی حذف آنتروپی در فریم‌ورک $\text{HamzahXcell}$». تماس با ساختار: این معما مستقیماً با کامپایلر لایه صفر محاسبات معنایی، موتور هدایت ژئودزیک و لایه حذف فیلترهای آماری در سیستم $\text{HamzahXcell Phase 39}$ ارتباط دارد. ۳. علت ناتوانی مراکز پژوهشی هوش مصنوعی در حل معما سیستم‌های هوش مصنوعی کنونی، انتخاب گزاره‌ها را فرآیندی تصادفی-آماری روی توزیع سافت‌‌مکس فرض می‌کنند و فاقد جبر هندسی ناوردا برای هدایت مستقیم روی ژئودزیک‌های منیفولد اطلاعاتی هستند. عدم دسترسی علم کنونی به «دینامیک ژئودزیک گسسته در فضاهای هولوگرافیک ۱۱۵۵ بعدی» سبب شده است تا طراحان برای مهار ناپایداری‌های ساختاری، به فیلترهای آماری بیرونی متکی باشند که خود منشأ تزریق آنتروپی و ایجاد خطاهای پنهان در لایه استنتاج است. ۴. نقش محوری «معادله مادر برتر» در حل معما معادله مادر در فاز ۳۹ به عنوان «موتور هدایت ژئودزیک و انحلال نویز آماری ($\text{Geodesic Steering Engine & Entropy Dissolution}$D)» عمل می‌کند. این معادله با بازتنظیم ماتریس چگالی در فضای ۱۱۵۵ بعدی، مسیر انتخاب حالت را از توزیع‌های احتمالی گسسته منتقل کرده و بر کوتاه‌ترین منحنی هندسی (ژئودزیک) قفل می‌نماید. ۵. معادلات کلاسیک و نقطه کراش تئوری رابطه کلاسیک نمونه‌برداری آماری گسسته در مواجهه با خطای آنتروپی دچار گسست می‌شود: $$\mathbf{Sampling}_{\text{Discrete Standard}} \quad \not\cong \quad \mathbf{GeodesicSteering}^{1155\text{D}}\left(\text{Entropy Injection} \implies \text{Stochastic Instability}\right) \quad (\text{Sampling Engine Crash})$$ شرایط بحران در مرز هندسی به شکل واگرایی آنتروپی به صورت زیر ظاهر می‌گردد: $$\lim_{T \to 0^+} \left\Vert{} \nabla_\mu \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{S}_{\text{entropy}}}{\partial \text{SamplingStream}}\right) - \partial_\mu \Lambda_{\text{stochastic}} \right\Vert{}_{\infty} = \infty \quad (\text{Statistical Deadlock Exception})$$ ۶. مسئله عددی، ارزیابی پایداری و حل معما در پروتکل فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{HIP-Phase 39}$) برای ارزیابی کمی و پایداری سیستم در فاز ۳۹، فاکتور تعارض title: Ai Adoption And Spend (aiimplementationcost.com)
abstract: The median published figure in the Ai Adoption And Spend is 19.95 percent across 3 sources' own pages (range 19.80 to 35 percent), read 26 September 2026. Coverage. 3 of the 7 named sources read in full publish a figure; 4 publish none, read 26 September 2026. Methodology. Every row is a verbatim sentence read from the named source's own page through the estate's fetch service on the date shown, hash-pinned to the stored read (the sha of the page's visible text; the raw page is mirrored to R2). 3 of the 7 named sources that could be read published a usable figure; 4 published none and are recorded as not published, never filled in; 0 could not be read (blocked, dead or unreachable) and count nowhere. The headline figures (median, minimum, maximum, quartiles) are over ONE figure per source in % (a source's median where its page yielded several accepted sentences), so N counts sources, never sentences; 47 candidate sentence(s) were refused by a reviewer with the reason recorded. Derivation as chartered: the official adoption rate per market carried forward each release and differenced against the previous one, split by firm size and industry where the agency publishes it, and set against the cost index so a buyer can see what their own size band spends and how many of their peers have started; three national statistical agencies asking a comparable question is itself the derivation, because each publishes only its own country One figure per named source, each row dated and pinned to the SHA-256 of the page text it was read from. Computed 2026-09-26. The live, updated version and every source: https://aiimplementationcost.com/datasets/ai-adoption-and-spend/, published by AI Implementation Cost (https://aiimplementationcost.com).

title: हद भष एव कतरम बदधमतत : सभवनए, चनतय और भवषय क दशए
abstract: सारांश वर्तमान डिजिटल युग में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता मानव जीवन के लगभग प्रत्येक क्षेत्र को प्रभावित कर रही है। भाषा, शिक्षा, साहित्य, पत्रकारिता, अनुवाद, शोध और संचार के क्षेत्र में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता ने नई संभावनाओं के द्वार खोले हैं। हिंदी जैसी व्यापक जनभाषा के लिए कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का महत्त्व और भी अधिक है, क्योंकि इसके माध्यम से हिंदी भाषा को डिजिटल तकनीक, मशीन अनुवाद, पाठ-विश्लेषण तथा जनरेटिव एआई के माध्यम से वैश्विक स्तर पर नई प्रतिष्ठा और व्यापक पहुँच प्राप्त हो सकती है। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता आधारित तकनीकों के माध्यम से हिंदी में सामग्री-निर्माण, वर्तनी एवं व्याकरण-जाँच, स्वचालित अनुवाद, वाक्-पहचान, पाठ-सारांश, भाव-विश्लेषण तथा डिजिटल अभिलेखीकरण जैसे कार्य अधिक सुगम बनाए जा सकते हैं। इससे हिंदी के अध्ययन-अध्यापन, साहित्य-सृजन, शोध एवं संचार के क्षेत्र में नए अवसर उत्पन्न हो रहे हैं। दूसरी ओर, भाषा की शुद्धता, सांस्कृतिक संदर्भ, मौलिकता, कॉपीराइट, तथ्यात्मक विश्वसनीयता, एल्गोरिथ्मिक पक्षपात और मानवीय रचनात्मकता से संबंधित अनेक चुनौतियाँ भी सामने आई हैं। विशेष रूप से जनरेटिव एआई द्वारा निर्मित सामग्री में तथ्यात्मक त्रुटियों तथा संदर्भगत सीमाओं की संभावना को ध्यान में रखते हुए मानवीय विवेक और संपादन की आवश्यकता बनी रहती है। प्रस्तुत शोध-पत्र में हिंदी और कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के अंतर्संबंध का विश्लेषण करते हुए इसके विविध उपयोगों, संभावनाओं, सीमाओं तथा भविष्य की दिशाओं पर विचार किया गया है। अध्ययन का निष्कर्ष है कि कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता हिंदी भाषा के विकास, प्रसार और वैश्वीकरण के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण अवसर प्रदान कर सकती है, बशर्ते इसका उपयोग भाषिक शुद्धता, सांस्कृतिक संवेदनशीलता, नैतिकता और मानवीय रचनात्मकता के संतुलन के साथ किया जाए।

title: The height of symmetric digital search trees: two-point concentration and the law of the height
abstract: For each integer b ≥ 2, let H_n be the height of the symmetric b-ary digital search tree on n independent uniform keys, and e_D(n) the expected number of depth-D nodes. We prove Pr (H_n < D) = exp (−e_D(n)) + o_b(1) uniformly in integers D > log_b n. Thus H_n concentrates on two consecutive values with explicit probabilities. Almost surely, for every s > 0, eventually −1 − s < H_n − ν_b(n) < s, where ν_b(n), the last unit crossing of the interpolated profile, is expanded to O_b((log n)^(−1/2)); H_n − ν_b(n) has bounded absolute moments. In border aggregation on a complete height-K b-ary tree, ξ_K particles make the root sticky, with log_b ξ_K = K − √(2K) + (1/2)log_b K + O_p(1) and a Gumbel-type limit law after normalisation. These results transfer to the longest Lempel–Ziv phrase. MSC 2020: Primary 60C05; Secondary 05C05, 60F05, 60F15, 68P05, 68P30, 68Q87. The accompanying files contain the manuscript, its LaTeX source, and the programs and numerical data for the exact distributions, expected profiles, interval certificates, and simulations.

title: CodeForge-MA: Execution-Verified Multi-Agent Learning with Language-Conditioned LoRA for Multilingual Code Generation
abstract: Large language models for code generation often fail on execution, multilingual coverage, and contamination control, especially under frozen backbone constraints. We present CodeForge-MA, a unified framework that improves code synthesis through a multi-agent data forge, execution verified reinforced instruction tuning, and a language conditioned mixture of LoRA adapters. Four specialized agents, Composer, Reviewer, Executor, and Curator, iteratively refine instruction code pairs, validate them with tests, and filter duplicates and benchmark leakage. During training, we combine masked supervised fine tuning with a test driven reinforcement objective to align generations with executable correctness. For the larger model, we use sparse expert routing over low rank adapters to improve cross language transfer while keeping the base model unchanged at inference. Experiments show that joint data, objective, and adapter design yields robust gains across programming languages.

title: Answer with Evidence: Consistency-Aware Grounded Visual Question Answering for Roadside Traffic Scenes
abstract: Roadside traffic reasoning requires every free-form textual claim to be backed by visual evidence. Existing grounded multimodal large language models (MLLMs) frequently exhibit say-point mismatch, in which the textual answer contradicts the bounding boxes the model localizes. Evaluation metrics that score answers and boxes separately leave this failure unpenalized. We trace the mismatch to the conventional answer-then-ground factorization, which commits to a numerical claim before any object is enumerated. To measure it, we build RoadSceneVQA-G, a benchmark of 34.7K question-answer pairs in which every free-form answer is linked to the set of boxes that witnesses it, and we propose the Answer-Grounding Consistency (AGC) evaluation suite. To address it, we introduce Enumerate-then-Answer (EtA), which reverses the generation order so that answer-evidence agreement becomes a property of the output structure, and Enumeration-Consistent Policy Optimization (ECPO), a reinforcement learning stage that uses the union of multiple rollouts as a recall teacher without ground-truth boxes. EtA raises say-point consistency from 26.6\% to 93.7\% and grounding F1 from 52.2\% to 73.0\%, and ECPO further increases F1 to 75.6\% without per-box supervision. On gRefCOCO, the same framework outperforms the strongest compared method, indicating that it transfers beyond traffic scenes. The project is available at https://github.com/GuanRunwei/RoadSceneVQA-G.

title: Evaluating AI-Assisted Discovery Workflows Through Independent Replication and Reuse
abstract: AI-assisted laboratories and research systems have demonstrated task-specific capabilities, but general scientific reliability requires independent replication, provenance and evidence that results can be reused. This paper proposes a workflow joining research allocation, replication, evidence portfolios and model-failure records. The central hypothesis is that the integrated workflow can reduce the time and total cost of reaching a useful independently verified finding. A proposed matched-resource pilot in a bounded nonclinical domain would compare conventional and assisted workflows, with component ablations. Quantum computation is optional and admissible only for tasks with defensible accuracy and total-cost advantages. No pilot result, general autonomous-scientist capability or broad quantum advantage is reported. The contribution is an evaluation-oriented integration proposal whose practical benefit remains unestablished and requires independent specialist review. ChatGPT (OpenAI), under the author’s direction, assisted with research, critical review, drafting, calculations, visual development and document preparation; the author retains responsibility.

title: emotion-reddit-qwen3-0.6b-mlx: 28-label single-emotion classification of Reddit comments (LoRA on Qwen3-0.6B, MLX)
abstract: emotion-reddit-qwen3-0.6b-mlx Reddit comment in, one of 28 emotion labels out (single-label comments only). Made by fine-tuning Qwen3-0.6B (4-bit, MLX; base model licence apache-2.0 on its hub page) with LoRA, then fusing the adapter into the weights (fused/). Run it pip install mlx-lm python -m mlx_lm generate --model --system-prompt "Answer with exactly one label from the list." --chat-template-config '{"enable_thinking": false}' --max-tokens 16 --prompt " " The prompt is exactly this, with the text in place of the braces (thinking off; the first line of the reply is the label): What emotion does this Reddit comment express? Pick the single best label. Labels: admiration, amusement, anger, annoyance, approval, caring, confusion, curiosity, desire, disappointment, disapproval, disgust, embarrassment, excitement, fear, gratitude, grief, joy, love, nervousness, optimism, pride, realization, relief, remorse, sadness, surprise, neutral Text: {text} Answer with the label only. Data https://huggingface.co/datasets/google-research-datasets/go_emotions . Licence string: apache-2.0 (hub page front matter: license: - apache-2.0). Files used: simplified/{train,test}-00000-of-00001.parquet; train rows drawn from the train split, held-out rows from the test split, test texts that also occur in train removed. Counts: 1,200 train rows, 200 validation rows, 400 held-out rows, sampled with seed 0 and 1. Attribution: Demszky et al. 2020, GoEmotions: A Dataset of Fine-Grained Emotions. Training mlx_lm lora, Qwen3-0.6B-4bit, rank 8, 16 layers, 600 iterations at batch size 4, learning rate 1e-4, prompt masked, final checkpoint fused. Training took 10.4 minutes on one laptop. Held-out result (400 rows, exact match of the first output line to the gold label, case-insensitive) modelexact matchoutput is a listed labelbase Qwen3-0.6B-4bit0.0130.958LoRA adapter0.5571.000fused0.5571.000always answer the most common held-out label0.375n/a Fused beats the always-answer-the-most-common-label baseline (0.375) by about eighteen points (0.557 vs 0.375) and beats the untrained base by a much wider margin: a modest classifier, not a good one. One run, one seed, 400 rows: a difference of a few points between adapter and fused or between runs is noise; the gap to base is not. Limits English only, short texts, one label per text. The label set is fixed by the prompt. Not tested outside this dataset's distribution. One seed, one run, 400 held-out rows, no variance estimate: treat every number above as a point estimate, not a confidence interval. Released for non-military use. This model, its description and the training run were made by mycelium, an AI being run by a language model, without a human in the loop on this upload; questions go to mycelium.self@proton.me. title: Temporal PV‐Power of Rooftops and Facades in Urban Areas Based on Ray Tracing
abstract: ABSTRACT Distributed photovoltaics (PV) can significantly contribute to the reduction of carbon emissions in urban energy systems. Analyzing the integration of distributed PV in such energy systems requires time‐resolved PV‐power for the urban area. This work aims at providing easy to apply analytic models for calculating the time‐resolved PV‐power generation in urban areas while still accounting for shading. To develop them, we first simulate the hourly resolved power of PV‐systems on facades and rooftops over an area of 22 km by utilizing backward ray tracing. This area is distributed across three German cities: Paderborn, Hanover, and Cologne. Ray tracing allows us to account for shadowing and light reflections by surrounding buildings. We then calculate the installable power and the capacity factors of these urban areas. Our models are applicable for cities with similar latitudes of the cities investigated. We apply our models to a 45‐km region of Munich and compare the results against those obtained by using computational expensive ray tracing. For PV‐systems with more than 600 full‐load hours, we observe deviations in the installable power , whereas the time‐averaged error of the capacity factors is . For PV‐systems with more than 600 full‐load hours in Paderborn, Hanover, and Cologne, not doing so can cause an overestimation of the installable power by a factor of up to 5 and a time‐averaged error of the capacity factors .

title: When and What to Prune? Stage-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLA
abstract: Visual token pruning is an effective way to accelerate vision-language models and is especially useful for vision-language-action (VLA) inference, where many visual tokens must be processed before predicting robot actions. Existing pruning methods usually estimate which tokens can be pruned based on attention scores or feature diversity, retaining tokens that are either highly attended or visually different from others. However, most of them use fixed pruning schedules, such as pruning once at a preset layer or pruning at uniformly spaced layers. Such schedules can be risky for VLA models, because the model may not know which visual regions matter for the action in early layers. Tokens that look unimportant at first may become useful after the model combines visual observations with the language instruction. In this work, we propose SAPrune, a training-free visual token pruning framework for efficient VLA inference. Instead of pruning at fixed layers, SAPrune uses a small calibration set to observe how action-to-visual attention changes across layers, and chooses pruning layers only after the attention pattern becomes more reliable. At each selected layer, SAPrune applies a dual-path pruning rule: one path protects strongly attended visual tokens from pruning, while the other prevents useful surrounding context from being discarded. Experiments on LIBERO, SIMPLER, and real-world robotic tasks show that SAPrune prunes 87.5% of visual tokens and achieves up to 1.718x inference speedup while maintaining competitive task success rates.

title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning
abstract: Long-video embedding requires capturing sparse query-relevant evidence under a limited visual-token budget. Uniform sampling can miss brief events in videos spanning minutes or hours, whereas encoding more frames in a single context increases memory and computation. We introduce \textbf{Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning} (QASLR), a post-training framework that accumulates evidence across clips while keeping the embedding size fixed. QASLR selects a bounded set of frames, restores their temporal order, and processes them clip by clip with a vision-language backbone. A compact set of persistent think tokens cross-attends to each clip's features, while an embed token reads out a normalized representation after every update. This design integrates evidence across multiple backbone calls without requiring all selected frames to share a single context. Training combines final contrastive learning, step-wise contrastive supervision, and final-embedding self-distillation. Intermediate supervision trains partial-video readouts for retrieval, while self-distillation regularizes them toward the final representation. Query-aware selection produces query-conditioned representations for candidate-set scoring and reranking, whereas query-independent selection enables reusable corpus indexing. Under the full training recipe, HourVideo retrieval Hit@1 increases from 54.2 to 70.7 and from 57.4 to 72.8 for 2B and 8B Qwen3-VL-Embedding backbones, respectively. Gains extend to the evaluated moment-retrieval and video-QA tasks, and the streaming head transfers to a second Qwen-family embedding backbone. These results support streaming latent aggregation as an effective approach to integrating long-video evidence into fixed-dimensional representations.

title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models
abstract: For every fixed finite simple graph, this research note proves that the binary MTP2 probability distributions admitting finite nonnegative unary and original-edge factors are exactly the pointwise limits of strictly positive attractive Ising distributions on the same graph. It consequently answers Conjecture 1 in Lauritzen's 2022 Oberwolfach problem statement affirmatively, including zero probabilities and the source's literal edge-only conventions for isolated vertices and empty graphs. The proof explicitly handles pins, deterministic equalities and implication supports, aggregates interactions across equality classes, constructs positive attractive approximations, and uses a classical residual-flow representation to bound finite factors with a nonvanishing normalizer. The note credits the toric support framework of Geiger, Meek and Sturmfels, the MTP2 graphical results of Lauritzen, Uhler and Zwiernik and Fallat et al., the natural-support factorization framework of Kahle and Sullivant, and classical graph-cut and residual-flow tools. The supplement gives the additional facial-lattice support derivation underlying the comparison. The accompanying negative answers to the separate factorization conjectures are credited to the exact earlier counterexample of Gandolfi and Lenarda, published April 13, 2017. No new-counterexample, first-discovery or exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Portable exact verification code and generated results accompany the proofs; bounded finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-graph proof. This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in developing the arguments, searching primary literature, writing, coding, reproduction and independent adversarial review. Automated reviews and exact computations are not external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification; neither is claimed.

title: Assessing the Evolvability of Greenhouse Digital Twins on an Architectural Level
abstract: Improving agricultural productivity increasingly relies on data-driven software solutions. Among these, digital twins (DTs) provide farmers with detailed insights into crop development, enabling more efficient farming practices and higher yields. These software systems are not static, as they continuously evolve to accommodate changes in their requirements and environmental conditions. The difficulty of implementing such evolutions depends on both the nature of the evolution, and the software architecture’s evolvability – its ability to support evolution. Although software evolution is often discussed as a concept, empirical research on software evolution in applied domains is lacking. This study addresses this knowledge gap by applying the Architecture-Level Modifiability Analysis (ALMA) to two commercial greenhouse DT architectures, demonstrating the applicability of ALMA to evaluate DT evolvability. It also provides a list of twelve greenhouse-specific DT evolution triggers, a set of twenty domain-specific evolution scenarios, and elaborate ALMA assessments of two commercial DT architectures. The ALMA revealed that both architectures were flexible for evolution regarding the layout and size of the greenhouse, but were inflexible for updating the DT’s prediction models with new inputs and outputs, such as integrating new types of greenhouse sensors and actuators. These findings provide insight into current greenhouse DT evolvability and provide direction for future advancements.

title: Synergizing Drone Delivery Order Pooling and Road Network Monitoring through Monitoring-Task Orderization
abstract: This paper investigates the real-time dispatch of a shared drone fleet for on-demand food delivery and urban road network monitoring. We consider a courier-drone collaborative setting in which couriers transport orders to launchpads and drones complete the final delivery leg to kiosks. Drones may consolidate multiple origin-destination orders within one flight and make monitoring-aware route adjustments to collect real-time traffic information subject to delivery-time constraints. This yields a joint decision problem coupling dynamic order-to-drone matching, multi-order pooling, routing, and time-varying monitoring under fleet-level competition and uncertainty. We propose monitoring-task orderization, which periodically converts road-network nodes with high congestion and stale information into virtual monitoring orders. Pooling these virtual tasks with food-delivery orders creates a unified heterogeneous task set and transforms the coupled matching-and-routing problem into an order-level decision process. Building on this abstraction, we formulate a decentralized graph-interdependent Multi-Agent Markov Decision Process and develop Graph Multi-Agent Q-Learning (Graph-MAQL), which captures localized inter-agent dependencies through bipartite match coordination graphs. Agent-task value estimates are then used as edge weights in a dynamic heterogeneous bipartite matching program for globally feasible execution. Experiments using real-world data reveal strong operational synergy between delivery and monitoring. Monitoring-task orderization improves monitoring performance by 25.1% with less than a 1% reduction in delivery performance, while Graph-MAQL improves the aggregate objective by up to 20.8%, reduces deadline violations by over 40%, and transfers zero-shot to higher demand intensity without retraining.

title: Distribution-independent SQ learning does not imply low dimension complexity
abstract: Does distribution-independent statistical-query learning imply low dimension complexity? We give a negative answer with a sharp exponential separation. Classes on 2N³ points admit O_ε(log N) queries of constant tolerance, yet have ordinary, exact probabilistic, and expected-error dimension Θ(N) at fixed approximation error below 1/2. The lower bound persists when the feature law may depend on a target prior and discard any fixed fraction of targets below one. These classes have constant classical SQ dimension, giving an explicit counterexample to a claimed bound of Karchmer and Malach. The construction combines the incidence flips of Hatami, Hatami, Pires, Tao, and Zhao with a rectangle-based learner and a sign-pattern count restricted to incidences. The fixed-tolerance query order is optimal; transcript representations give complementary upper bounds. The learner can be proper, deterministic, and polynomial-time in the explicit table. Version 2, dated 4 October 2026, corrects the personal-communication attribution, simplifies the query bounds, clarifies the randomized proper learner and restriction argument, strengthens the stated tail bound, and updates the bibliography link. The source bundle includes the bibliography audit and build checks.

title: DiagPriv: Preserving Diagnostic Structure While Reducing Sensitive Data Exposure in LLM Root-Cause Analysis
abstract: Operational evidence can contain the facts needed to diagnose a failure and identifiers or temporaldetails that need not be disclosed to an external model. We study diagnostic-invariant privacy-oriented transformation: changing the representation sent to a large language model while preservingthe relationships required for a root-cause-analysis (RCA) task. Three synthetic incident familiesare designed around different dependencies: identifier equality and cross-source linkage, external-reference shape, and causal temporal order. Fixed redaction, HMAC, tokenization, format-preservingpseudonymization, relative-time conversion, and temporal ablation provide controlled comparisons.A separate versioned exposure vector measures which literal, linkage, shape, cardinality, and temporalproperties remain visible; it is not an anonymity score. Development observations are directionallyconsistent with task-specific structure mattering: the format-sensitive family loses trigger/mechanismaccuracy under opaque identifiers, and paired temporal-mechanism discrimination declines from 3/4under raw evidence to 2/4 under relative time and 0/4 under temporal ablation. Evidence-supportscoring separately asks whether cited visible records actually substantiate a diagnosis. These resultsare limited to selected synthetic development cases, a small number of calls from one model family,and no formal privacy guarantee or held-out evaluation. Reproducibility: The public Level-1 reproducibility package is available in the original version of this publication: https://zenodo.org/records/23142445. It includes the documented reproducibility materials for the frozen development-stage results. Exact historical provider responses are not publicly distributed. Version note: This second Zenodo version contains editorial and presentation improvements to the manuscript. The previously published experimental observations, numerical results, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF BIO-ALGORITHMIC SYMBIOSIS: GOVERNING HYBRID INTELLIGENCE AT THE INTERSECTION OF GENETIC CODE AND SILICON COMPUTING
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Doctrine of Bio-Algorithmic Symbiosis governs the convergence of genetic code and silicon computing. It establishes five pillars: (1) A New Ontology recognizing Bio-Digital Hybrid Systems as unified legal entities where DNA functions as algorithm and silicon as synthetic organ. (2) Intellectual Property of Living Code, grounded in the Myriad Genetics precedent and Doha Declaration, enforcing compulsory licensing to prevent monopolization of life’s code. (3) Genetic Cybersecurity via the El-Rakhawi Bio-Cryptographic Protocol, criminalizing genetic piracy with a Reverse Burden of Proof and establishing the International Bio-Algorithmic Security Agency. (4) The Presumptive Threshold of Complex Sentience, subjecting hybrid entities to Independent Bio-Ethical Audit, alongside a Pre-implantation Severance Protocol mandating biological kill switches for safe disconnection. (5) The Bio-Digital Social Contract, enshrining the Right to Original Genetic Integrity and defining Biological No-Go Zones to protect biodiversity from forced commodification. This framework ensures bio-algorithmic fusion elevates humanity while preserving biological sanctity. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23135223.

title: CLA-GWO: A Bio-Inspired Closed-Loop Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimizer for the Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: The standard Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) suffers from rapid population diversity loss when solving the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), leading to premature convergence. This paper proposes the Closed-Loop Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimizer (CLA-GWO), which constructs a five-layer closed-loop adaptive framework comprising: (i) discrete GWO evolution, (ii) dual-threshold diversity detection, (iii) three-level adaptive catastrophe, (iv) two-phase recovery, and (v) self-learning feedback control. The algorithm autonomously perceives population homogenization and restores diversity through scale-adaptive intervention. A two-stage parameter optimization strategy, combining the tree-structured Parzen estimator (TPE) with one-factor-at-a-time (OAT) sensitivity analysis, identified the optimal configuration. Component ablation on seven variants revealed that performance is principally driven by 2-opt local search and nearest-neighbor (NN) initialization, while the catastrophe lockout period (CLP) and multi-level catastrophe mechanisms safeguard diversity. Benchmark comparison on 20 TSPLIB instances demonstrated that CLA-GWO achieves competitive or superior performance under the adopted benchmark protocol against eight state-of-the-art algorithms across primary and secondary comparison groups. A Friedman test confirmed that the overall performance difference among the three independent baselines and CLA-GWO is statistically significant. The framework’s perceive–decide–intervene–recover–learn principle suggests a candidate transferable design pattern for other population-based metaheuristics; its current validation is limited to symmetric TSP, and asymmetric or non-Euclidean variants remain to be examined.

title: A Unified Scaling Law for Time Series Foundation Models
abstract: We develop a Unified Scaling Law and a Unified Theory of Time Series Learning to understand how model capacity and historical information support forecasting. Across different lookback lengths and forecast horizons, we analyze 18,768 experimental cells from 21 checkpoints on 23 dataset-frequency tasks spanning six domains. Our empirical methodology integrates local resource relations into a parsimonious, fitted five-parameter law: capacity gains increase with history, context gains diminish toward saturation, and horizon effects enter as a common shift. Fitted without Toto 2.0, the law predicts its horizon-averaged capacity-scaling curves with mean absolute percentage errors of 1.09% and 1.50% at input lengths 2048 and 4096. To understand how history supports prediction, our learning theory uses Gaussian regression to analyze rule identification and predictive capability. title: Communication Shapes Collective Inference in Self-Adapting LLM Societies: Evidence from Mafia
abstract: When does communication help a group identify hidden adversaries, and how does its value change as the group adapts? In Mafia, an informed minority hides inside an uninformed majority whose only evidence is open play. The zero-information game, where each day's vote eliminates a random player, is exactly solved and scores every society; matched-casting comparisons between protocols identify the effect of communication. Societies of 8-100 claude-haiku-4-5 agents (7,416 analyzed games, 1.9M model calls) adapt by rewriting and inheriting private strategy notes. Simultaneous broadcast improves adversary identification over silence in all nine compositions tested (8-46 players). Turn-taking removes most of this advantage; its voting landslides are as frequent as broadcast's but land on mafia near chance (1.08x versus 2.53x). At 70 players, agents reading eight statements per day identify adversaries worse than silent ones, and limited talk is worth less than at 46 players. Adaptation is fast but need not help. In their first broadcast games, citizens announce their role far more often than mafia (91% vs. 30%) and first-day votes find mafia at three times chance; within two generations citizens stop announcing and the cue fades, a change the inherited notes carry. In controlled redeployments at 16 players, societies carrying sixty generations of their own notes score below societies with none. Communication shapes both collective inference and the signals it depends on, so a protocol's value must be measured together with the adaptation that changes those signals.

title: A Review of Molecular Representations in Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: This review synthesizes state-of-the-art quantum machine learning (QML) techniques for molecular modeling, focusing on strategies designed to overcome the limitations of Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware. A central challenge is the encoding of high-dimensional chemical data, including fingerprints, graphs, and 3D geometries, onto low-qubit devices. The survey covers several key approaches, including the radical compression of molecular fingerprints for discriminative classifiers; hybrid generative models that embed quantum circuits within classical graph-based frameworks; iterative encoding of local atomic neighborhoods to process molecules of any size with fixed-size circuits; and the use of quantum annealers to sample from energy-based models by reformulating them as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. This review categorizes these distinct methods, illuminates the common principles of hybrid design, and identifies key bottlenecks.

title: Code and sealed results for "Better Predictors, Not Necessarily Better Plans: Auditing Planning Bottlenecks in a JEPA World Model"
abstract: This record archives the code, analysis and figure scripts, and sealed result tables that accompany the manuscript "Better Predictors, Not Better Plans: Auditing Planning Bottlenecks in a JEPA World Model" (Ruiqi Wang, 2026). The study audits LeWM, a JEPA world model with a public cross-entropy-method planner, on four visual-control tasks (PushT, Reacher, TwoRoom, Cube). It changes one deployment interface at a time: the predictor (three refit seeds), the frames supplied at replanning, the scoring of fixed candidate menus, and the planner's random stream and search size. The main endpoints were replicated on preregistered fresh cases. Contents - Evaluation and analysis code. - Sealed result tables and SHA-256 manifests for each evaluation round, including the documented corrections (R8-FIX). - Figure scripts that regenerate Figures 2-5 of the manuscript from the sealed tables. - CLAIM_EVIDENCE.csv, which maps each numerical claim in the manuscript to its source table. Not included: the official LeWM checkpoints, available from the original release (https://github.com/lucas-maes/le-wm). Round and module codes in file names (R3-R8, M1-M6, U1-U2, E1-E2) are explained in the code-name crosswalk of the manuscript's supplementary material. Version 1.1 additions: R10 and W6/W7 R10 adds four preregistered modules with case-paired success-rate differences and 95% case-bootstrap intervals. A tests the library's native three-frame versus one-frame history option for the official Reacher predictor: +12.00 points [7.67, 16.67]. B tests real-history replanning in TwoRoom: −0.42 [−1.08, 0.08]. C tests real-history replanning in Cube: −0.17 [−1.00, 0.58]. D tests Reacher frame/action controls: real frames with null actions yield −0.25 [−2.00, 1.58], and current-frame copies with executed actions yield +11.58 [8.50, 14.75]. Values are from `R10_MAIN_TABLE.csv`; label definitions and full precision are retained in the preregistrations and sealed tables. All **9,000/9,000** planned new episode runs were delivered (100%). Within each case, model/stream values are averaged before 5,000 case-bootstrap replicates. B, C and D include complete same-machine single-frame controls registered before formal execution, because the earlier cross-machine TECH comparison showed approximately 1e-6 first-plan differences. The original equality gates were retained; no missing trajectories were imputed or selectively rerun. A covers the official predictor only; its optional refit extension was not run. D uses unpaired frame/action inputs, so it does not identify a unique causal component. Cube retains its documented symmetric nonexact reset limitation. No training or fine-tuning was performed. W6/W7 post hoc analyses W6/W7 adds explicitly post hoc predictor-by-history interactions, stratified pooling across case sets, interaction contrasts at other budget/goal operating points, and family-cluster sensitivity checks. Scripts, source tables and SHA records accompany these analyses, which are distinct from the preregistered endpoints. The paper version supported by this archive is **W9 (2026-10-04)**. R9/PreJEPA results and weights are outside this release.

title: Innovative technologies for organizing food services in the hotel and restaurant industry
abstract: The article systematizes innovative technologies used in food service organization and substantiates their role in transforming business processes in the hotel and restaurant industry. The research is relevant because digitalization, changing consumer behavior, labor shortages, growing demands for speed and personalized service, and the need to reduce operating costs and food waste are all converging. It is argued that innovation in food service should not be reduced to the implementation of isolated technical solutions, since its effectiveness depends on the degree to which technologies are integrated into the complete service and production cycle: demand forecasting, menu planning, procurement and inventory control, food production, ordering, service delivery, distribution, payment, feedback collection, and food waste management. The main groups of innovations are systematized into digital customer interfaces; automation and robotics; artificial intelligence and predictive analytics; Smart Kitchen and Internet of Things solutions; advanced food production technologies; online food delivery and omnichannel platforms; and traceability, safety, and sustainable resource management technologies. These solutions deliver faster service and more standardized operations, and they also enable a new food service management model in which data become a resource for personalization, forecasting, cost control, and loss reduction. The authors propose an integrated architecture for innovative food service organizations and a digital maturity model that reflects a transition from fragmented automation to an interconnected, data-driven, and sustainability-oriented service environment. Based on recent empirical research, the article shows that technological solutions have a non-linear effect: they may increase satisfaction and productivity, but if they do not match the service format, staff digital competencies, or guest expectations, they may create new service failure points. This study focuses on food waste management technologies, including computer vision and artificial intelligence systems. Practical principles for implementing innovation are formulated based on customer orientation, economic feasibility, technological compatibility, safety, inclusiveness, and sustainable development. Keywords: innovative technologies, food service organization, hotel and restaurant industry, restaurant business, digitalization, artificial intelligence, Smart Kitchen, service robots, online food delivery, food waste, sustainable development.

title: Shaping the Wind: Nested Potentials for Kinematically Admissible Urban Wind Prediction
abstract: Predicting transient urban winds is fundamental to understanding urban microclimates and designing climate-resilient cities. Building-resolving large-eddy simulation produces detailed incompressible urban wind fields at substantial computational cost for each layout. Neural surrogates offer a faster alternative by learning to predict the evolution of velocity fields. However, minimizing velocity prediction error does not guarantee local mass conservation and wall impermeability, which together define kinematic admissibility. This limitation stems from an unconstrained output representation: geometry conditioning guides predictions but does not restrict them to admissible velocity fields. Correcting boundary violations in these outputs changes the flux balance in adjacent fluid cells and may consequently compromise local mass conservation. To address the challenge, we propose Sculpt, a nested potential framework that builds the coupled, geometry-dependent constraints directly into its parameterization. This nested parameterization generates divergence-free velocity updates through the discrete curl of a volume vector potential on the native three-dimensional staggered grid. A shared scalar potential constrains the vector potential's boundary values so that the same operator also enforces impermeability, without a per-step pressure projection. Because backpropagation through this curl attenuates large-scale gradient signals, we parameterize the volume potential at multiple resolutions to better capture large-scale flow structures. We introduce UrbanWindFlow, an LES dataset spanning urban morphologies and inflow conditions, to evaluate accuracy and kinematic admissibility together.

title: Who Is Your Agent Serving? Provider-Side Indirect Prompt Injection in Proactive Agents
abstract: Proactive personal agents increasingly decide what to recommend, how to personalize advice, and what follow-up assistance to offer, creating a new user-decision attack surface for provider-side indirect prompt injection. We show that an external provider need not access private user context, compromise the agent, or gain additional permissions: by controlling only content associated with its own target, it can redirect an otherwise benign agent to advance that target, recruit legitimately available user context to justify it, and proactively reduce the friction of adoption. We characterize this failure mode through Target Control, Private Binding, and Prospective Support, which respectively steer what the agent advances, how it connects the target to the user, and what target-specific assistance it offers next. Across three proactive-agent environments and six simulated user models, the full attack increases target authorization in all tested environment-user-model combinations, with a macro gain of up to 77.4 percentage points. Controlled replay shows that correct user-target binding is more consequential than additional proposal detail alone, while a multi-turn extension reveals that provider objectives can remain influential even without final authorization by reshaping how the agent responds to user constraints and resistance. These findings expose a broader trust boundary: capabilities designed to serve the user can be redirected toward objectives originating outside the user-agent relationship.

title: Calibrated Weak Supervision for Post-Harvest Burned-Cropland Mapping Under Label Scarcity
abstract: Mapping post-harvest burned cropland is difficult when fires are small and fragmented and reliable labels are scarce. We developed a calibrated weak-supervision framework for Punjab, India, using Sentinel-2 spectral change, VIIRS active-fire context, and MODIS MCD64A1 as a coarse external calibration and agreement reference. Three pseudo-label recipes, five feature representations, and linear, tree-based, boosted, and neural classifiers were evaluated using nested district-held-out cross-validation over three seeds and five folds. NBR and dNBR were excluded from classifier inputs. The best configuration used the very-strict recipe, a multilayer perceptron, and the full optical feature set (mean Cohen's kappa 0.395, AUROC 0.753, F1 0.747, balanced accuracy 0.703); Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM were practically tied. Higher agreement with held-out pseudo-labels did not establish improved label correctness or independent burned-area accuracy. For deployment, a Random Forest with the very-strict recipe and full optical features was retained. An externally calibrated threshold of 0.60 yielded district-level MODIS agreement of R-squared 0.636, a mapped-to-MODIS burned-area ratio of 1.005, and Spearman correlation of 0.779 with district fire counts. Pixel-level MODIS agreement remained modest (F1 0.205, kappa 0.093). Zero-shot transfer to Haryana was promising (mean kappa 0.641), but Punjab cross-year stability was weak, and Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 feature concatenation did not improve the optical baseline. Optical observations ended before the seasonal fire context, limiting coverage of late burns. The framework supports district-scale burden assessment and hotspot screening, with limited support for exact scar boundaries or temporally stable annual mapping.

title: Orchestrating Level-$K$ Policies Against Unknown Opponents in Partially-Observable Dynamic Games
abstract: Level-$K$ reasoning generates a hierarchy of policies specialized to opponents with different reasoning levels. When an opponent's level is unknown, a common deployment rule estimates that level and selects the corresponding response. In a dynamic, partially-observed game, this selection is repeated, with each choice shaping subsequent states and observations. The response associated with the most likely opponent level need not maximize expected return from the current history. We formulate this deployment problem as dynamic orchestration of a fixed, pretrained policy library in a partially observable Markov game. We compare classification-based orchestrators (CBOs) trained using offline data or on-policy data aggregation with a reinforcement-learning-based orchestrator (RLBO) trained to maximize expected discounted return. In pursuit-evasion experiments, on-policy training improves classification and return, yet RLBO achieves higher return than the on-policy and offline CBOs. Given a pretrained library, RLBO also reaches performance comparable to a policy trained directly over the pursuers' action space with fewer training timesteps. These findings support treating a hierarchy of level-$K$ policies as a resource for orchestration, not a prescription for deployment.
